Friends, but make it easy

Friendships are made on Meetup

Since 2002, members have used Meetup to make new friends, meet like-minded people, spend time on hobbies, and connect with locals over shared interests.

I used Meetup to make friends at brunch

New Jersey-based writer Brianna Stryker wanted to meet friends in her hometown. Learn how she used Meetup to make connections by joining a Girls Night Out Meetup group.

How to turn casual connections into close friendships

It’s proven that close friendships are harder to make as an adult. But don’t sweat it: here’s what you can do to simplify the process.

Do you have the “right” number of friends?

Studies from around the world have tried to help people answer this question. Learn about the three tiers of friendship and how to fulfill them.

<p>If you’ve ever wondered if you have the “right” number of friends, you’re not alone. Several different research studies reported in the <em>New York Times</em> have aimed to figure out if an ideal number of social connections exists. </p>



<p>At first blush, it may seem odd to analyze your social circle in this way, but it’s actually relevant to your overall health. <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/07/well/live/adult-friendships-number.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Friendship in the United States has been on the decline for decades</a>, and the pandemic put that trend into overdrive. The result of shrinking social circles is an increase in loneliness and isolation—emotional struggles that can have notable physical effects, such as higher risk of depression, substance abuse, stress disorders, heart disease, and stroke. </p>



<p>On the other hand, there is also an upper limit to how many friendships you can realistically maintain. If you spread yourself too thin, trying to make yourself available to too many people, you may encounter serious anxiety, forgetfulness, lack of productivity, and emotional turbulence. </p>



<p>With all of that in mind, it’s important to reflect on your social life and see if it could use some adjusting. A simple way to do this is by breaking down your connections into three main groups: casual friends, consistent friends, and close friends. </p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-the-three-types-of-friends-and-how-to-make-them">The three types of friends and how to make them   </h2>



<p>It goes without saying that all friendships are unique, but for the purpose of organizing them in your head and judging your own social satisfaction, they can be broadly categorized into three tiers.  </p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-casual-friends">Casual friends  </h3>



<p>A casual friend is someone whose contact info you have, but you don’t regularly stay in touch. They may just be a friendly acquaintance, or even a coworker you get along with. They could be someone you don’t know all that well, but who you met for a particular reason, like a shared hobby.   </p>



<p>Although casual friendships are the least intimate of the three categories, they are also the easiest to make! Ideally, you should have a few casual friends for all the activities you enjoy and settings you spend a lot of time in. </p>



<p>If you’re a bookworm, try seeking out a community like <a href="https://www.meetup.com/the-book-buffet/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Book Buffet</a> in San Diego where you can casually connect over a love of literature while relaxing in the park. If getting active is your thing, find a community like the <a href="https://www.meetup.com/chicagohos/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Chicago Hiking, Outdoors, & Social Group</a> that does everything from birdwatching and biking to canoeing and camping. No matter where you are, your best bet for making new casual connections is by attending a Meetup event.  </p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-consistent-friends">Consistent friends  </h3>



<p>They may not be your best friend, but a consistent friend is someone you’re in regular contact with. You can frequently rely on them for a good chat or a fun outing, and you know each other on a more personal level.  </p>



<p>A handful of these types of friends—five or so—is a good estimate for the amount of consistent connection you can sustain. The best way to <a href="https://www.meetup.com/blog/meetup-product-release-notes/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">make consistent friends</a> is by deepening some of the relationships you already have with casual friends, a select few who you really vibe with.  </p>



<p>Put in the time to grow your casual friendship into something more. You could try making plans to get coffee, or having a few people over for dinner. You could even host a party! It’s easy to strengthen your connections when the conversation’s flowing, every guest feels included, and there’s an almost magical buzz in the air. All you have to do is follow these tips on <a href="https://www.meetup.com/blog/how-to-throw-a-great-party/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">how to throw a great party</a>. </p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-close-friends">Close friends   </h3>



<p>A close friend is someone you can always rely on, and someone who knows they can always rely on you. Really, this kind of connection goes beyond friendship—they’re a confidant you can trust, someone who helps you go through the highs and lows of life. </p>



<p>You should have at least one close friend, but it doesn’t hurt to have a couple more. Just keep in mind that it’s unsustainable to try being this close with all of your friends.    </p>



<p>Once again, you can develop close friendships by drawing on already established relationships, but this time try deepening a connection with a consistent friend. Pick someone who you sense is honest and willing to be vulnerable, and whose company makes you feel full rather than depleted. A close friendship can even be rekindled with an old friend you’ve fallen out of touch with, or a family member you want to establish a deeper relationship with. </p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-putting-yourself-out-there">Putting yourself out there  </h2>



<p>The hardest part is often the most rewarding. It’s tempting to stay in your comfort zone, but that’s not where real personal growth happens, and it’s certainly not where you’re going to discover lots of new connections. The key to putting yourself out there is making sure “out there” is full of people who share your interests. The best way to do that is by attending Meetup events! You can even <a href="https://www.meetup.com/lp/how-to-group-start/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">create your own Meetup group</a> and invite <a href="https://www.meetup.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">potential friends near you </a>to join an activity you love.</p>

https://www.meetup.com/blog/do-you-have-.visible_text: --> --> --> Do You Have the “Right” Number of Friends? - Meetup Blog Community Matters Organizer Guide Product Updates Keep Connected Podcast Meetup Live Local Guides Get the newsletter Categories Organizer Guide Product Updates Keep Connected Podcast Meetup Live Local Guides Get Updates Get the newsletter Stories Do You Have the “Right” Number of Friends? Studies from around the world have tried to help people answer this question. Learn about the three tiers of friendship and how to fulfill them. By James Quigley Share If you’ve ever wondered if you have the “right” number of friends, you’re not alone. Several different research studies reported in the New York Times have aimed to figure out if an ideal number of social connections exists.  At first blush, it may seem odd to analyze your social circle in this way, but it’s actually relevant to your overall health. Friendship in the United States has been on the decline for decades , and the pandemic put that trend into overdrive. The result of shrinking social circles is an increase in loneliness and isolation—emotional struggles that can have notable physical effects, such as higher risk of depression, substance abuse, stress disorders, heart disease, and stroke.  On the other hand, there is also an upper limit to how many friendships you can realistically maintain. If you spread yourself too thin, trying to make yourself available to too many people, you may encounter serious anxiety, forgetfulness, lack of productivity, and emotional turbulence.  With all of that in mind, it’s important to reflect on your social life and see if it could use some adjusting. A simple way to do this is by breaking down your connections into three main groups: casual friends, consistent friends, and close friends.  The three types of friends and how to make them    It goes without saying that all friendships are unique, but for the purpose of organizing them in your head and judging your own social satisfaction, they can be broadly categorized into three tiers.   Casual friends   A casual friend is someone whose contact info you have, but you don’t regularly stay in touch. They may just be a friendly acquaintance, or even a coworker you get along with. They could be someone you don’t know all that well, but who you met for a particular reason, like a shared hobby.    Although casual friendships are the least intimate of the three categories, they are also the easiest to make! Ideally, you should have a few casual friends for all the activities you enjoy and settings you spend a lot of time in.  If you’re a bookworm, try seeking out a community like The Book Buffet in San Diego where you can casually connect over a love of literature while relaxing in the park. If getting active is your thing, find a community like the Chicago Hiking, Outdoors, & Social Group that does everything from birdwatching and biking to canoeing and camping. No matter where you are, your best bet for making new casual connections is by attending a Meetup event.   Consistent friends   They may not be your best friend, but a consistent friend is someone you’re in regular contact with. You can frequently rely on them for a good chat or a fun outing, and you know each other on a more personal level.   A handful of these types of friends—five or so—is a good estimate for the amount of consistent connection you can sustain. The best way to make consistent friends is by deepening some of the relationships you already have with casual friends, a select few who you really vibe with.   Put in the time to grow your casual friendship into something more. You could try making plans to get coffee, or having a few people over for dinner. You could even host a party! It’s easy to strengthen your connections when the conversation’s flowing, every guest feels included, and there’s an almost magical buzz in the air. All you have to do is follow these tips on how to throw a great party .  Close friends    A close friend is someone you can always rely on, and someone who knows they can always rely on you. Really, this kind of connection goes beyond friendship—they’re a confidant you can trust, someone who helps you go through the highs and lows of life.  You should have at least one close friend, but it doesn’t hurt to have a couple more. Just keep in mind that it’s unsustainable to try being this close with all of your friends.     Once again, you can develop close friendships by drawing on already established relationships, but this time try deepening a connection with a consistent friend. Pick someone who you sense is honest and willing to be vulnerable, and whose company makes you feel full rather than depleted. A close friendship can even be rekindled with an old friend you’ve fallen out of touch with, or a family member you want to establish a deeper relationship with.  Putting yourself out there   The hardest part is often the most rewarding. It’s tempting to stay in your comfort zone, but that’s not where real personal growth happens, and it’s certainly not where you’re going to discover lots of new connections. The key to putting yourself out there is making sure “out there” is full of people who share your interests. The best way to do that is by attending Meetup events! You can even create your own Meetup group and invite potential friends near you to join an activity you love. **A Guided Online Meet-Up for Clarity & Direction**
Many of us are doing “all the right things”, working hard, staying responsible, moving forward, yet still feel disconnected or unsure about why we are doing what we do.
This guided online meet-up is designed to help you pause, reflect, and gain **clear direction**, not through motivation or advice, but through **structured self-inquiry**.

## What to Expect

This is a **facilitated, reflective session** where you will:

* Explore your **long-term purpose direction**
* Identify what truly matters to you in this phase of life
* Translate clarity into **short-term, actionable priorities**
* Leave with a grounded understanding of where your energy belongs next

The session is thoughtful, respectful, and practical, not motivational or spiritual in nature.

## Agenda & Flow

**1\. Setting the Context**
Why purpose feels confusing today and what clarity actually means
**2\. Long\-Term Vision \(Ikigai Framework\)**
Understanding purpose through:

* What you love
* What you are good at
* What the world needs
* What you can be valued for

**3\. Short\-Term Direction \(Passion Test\)**

* Identifying current priorities
* Converting purpose into 90-day focus areas

**4\. Integration & Reflection**
Connecting long-term direction with short-term action
**5\. Closing & Q&A**
Personal questions will be addressed toward the end

## You Will Walk Away With

* A clear **purpose direction**
* Priority focus for the **next 90 days**
* Reduced confusion in life and career decisions
* A grounded action plan you can realistically follow

## What to Bring

* A notebook or digital notes
* Openness to reflect honestly
* Willingness to engage when invited, no pressure to overshare

No prior knowledge or preparation is required.

## Session Guidelines

* Personal comments are avoided during the session
* Personal questions will be taken at the end
* Please avoid side or private chats
* Participation in reflections is encouraged when invited

* This is an **online live session**
* The joining link will be shared with registered attendees before the event
* Please join on time to get the full experience

About this meetup.......

I don't want to stereotype any age group because in my opinion nearly everyone involved in the mainstream crowd these days is a little crazy. I'll thank social media and Covid-19 for that. LOL!

I'm the kind of guy that just likes to mind this own business, say "Ok" to controversial stuff to avoid problems, and remember the old days to stay mentally healthy. **Hi there! My name is Chloe.**
I'm a certified English teacher from United States.
I wanted to make an online language club where people can practice foreign languages by having real casual conversation!
I'm looking for people who want to practice conversational English by talking about interesting topics and hanging out with people from all over the world in a small online group.
**Here are some examples of what our weekly topics might be like:**
**"What would you do if you come across your crush?"**
**"Have you ever done the MBTI test? If so, what is your personality type?"**
**"Do you believe in love at first sight? Why or why not?"**
**"What are you most worried about right now?**
💎Here are some details💎
✔️ We meet via Zoom
✔️ The session will last for 1 hour and consists of 3 different rounds
✔️ Each round has different topics and discussion questions
✔️ Each round, the groups are randomly mixed, so you will have a chance to talk to different people every time
✔️ This isn't just about practicing English, but also about listening to different opinions and learning about different cultures
**✔️ The participation is FREE**
**❌ No credit card**
**❌ No Ads**

**📢IMPORTANT : CHECK THE SESSION TIME IN OUR WEBSITE(The time on the website and the meetup site may not match since we change it ocasionally)**

💎 How to Join 💎

1. [Click the link(here)](https://langclub.live/sessions)
2. [Sign up](https://langclub.live/signup)

3\. Click 'book' in the session that you want to participate\.
4\. Show up at the session time and click 'Join' in the session page
(The Zoom invitation will be sent to your e-mail once you apply too)
5\. Enjoy practicing English with people from all over the world\!

Your Purpose","description":"## Find Your Purpose

**A Guided Online Meet-Up for Clarity & Direction**
Many of us are doing “all the right things”, working hard, staying responsible, moving forward, yet still feel disconnected or unsure about why we are doing what we do.
This guided online meet-up is designed to help you pause, reflect, and gain **clear direction**, not through motivation or advice, but through **structured self-inquiry**.

## What to Expect

This is a **facilitated, reflective session** where you will:

* Explore your **long-term purpose direction**
* Identify what truly matters to you in this phase of life
* Translate clarity into **short-term, actionable priorities**
* Leave with a grounded understanding of where your energy belongs next

The session is thoughtful, respectful, and practical, not motivational or spiritual in nature.

## Agenda & Flow

**1\. Setting the Context**
Why purpose feels confusing today and what clarity actually means
**2\. Long\-Term Vision \(Ikigai Framework\)**
Understanding purpose through:

* What you love
* What you are good at
* What the world needs
* What you can be valued for

**3\. Short\-Term Direction \(Passion Test\)**

* Identifying current priorities
* Converting purpose into 90-day focus areas

**4\. Integration & Reflection**
Connecting long-term direction with short-term action
**5\. Closing & Q&A**
Personal questions will be addressed toward the end

## You Will Walk Away With

* A clear **purpose direction**
* Priority focus for the **next 90 days**
* Reduced confusion in life and career decisions
* A grounded action plan you can realistically follow

## What to Bring

* A notebook or digital notes
* Openness to reflect honestly
* Willingness to engage when invited, no pressure to overshare

No prior knowledge or preparation is required.

## Session Guidelines

To keep the space respectful and focused:

* Personal comments are avoided during the session
* Personal questions will be taken at the end
* Please avoid side or private chats
* Participation in reflections is encouraged when invited

## How to Join

* This is an **online live session**
* The joining link will be shared with registered attendees before the event
* Please join on time to get the full experience

**Facilitated by:**

**Hi there! My name is Chloe.**
I'm a certified English teacher from United States.
I wanted to make an online language club where people can practice foreign languages by having real casual conversation!
I'm looking for people who want to practice conversational English by talking about interesting topics and hanging out with people from all over the world in a small online group.
**Here are some examples of what our weekly topics might be like:**
**"What would you do if you come across your crush?"**
**"Have you ever done the MBTI test? If so, what is your personality type?"**
**"Do you believe in love at first sight? Why or why not?"**
**"What are you most worried about right now?**
💎Here are some details💎
✔️ We meet via Zoom
✔️ The session will last for 1 hour and consists of 3 different rounds
✔️ Each round has different topics and discussion questions
✔️ Each round, the groups are randomly mixed, so you will have a chance to talk to different people every time
✔️ This isn't just about practicing English, but also about listening to different opinions and learning about different cultures
**✔️ The participation is FREE**
**❌ No credit card**
**❌ No Ads**

**📢IMPORTANT : CHECK THE SESSION TIME IN OUR WEBSITE(The time on the website and the meetup site may not match since we change it ocasionally)**

💎 How to Join 💎

1. [Click the link(here)](https://langclub.live/sessions)
2. [Sign up](https://langclub.live/signup)

3\. Click 'book' in the session that you want to participate\.
4\. Show up at the session time and click 'Join' in the session page
(The Zoom invitation will be sent to your e-mail once you apply too)
5\. Enjoy practicing English with people from all over the world\!

Sign up for Online English classes with English for Asia. Improve your English. Build confidence in speaking! We offer regular English lessons at a very affordable price (FREE!).

Select your classes here: https://englishforasia.zoom.us/ze/hub/TESOL/events

Lessons include speaking, listening, reading, writing, grammar and pronunciation. All lessons are taught by trainee teachers who are observed by master teacher trainers from Trinity College London.

Classes are for people aged 18 years old and above (IST / Mondays to Saturdays).

For the best experience, attendees should have:

* a computer or ipad style device (no phones please)
* stable internet access
* a headset with microphone
* a webcam

All online lessons are free!

By joining the class you agree:
1\. not to record the lesson
2\. not to use offensive language
3\. not to display obscene material
4\. not to share phishing links

Please call or WhatsApp +85297232290 if you have any questions or connection issues.

jsonld_parsed.name: Nostalgia: Let's listen to some older songs and remember the old days
jsonld_parsed.description:
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*
Update: the **un**official meetup **will still happen** **tonight**, but the **official** meetup date will again be forwarded to a later date. After you RSVP you'll be able to find the Google Meet link for tonight, **Sep 4, 2026**, at 7 pm Thailand time / 8 pm Hong Kong time.
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*

About this meetup.......

I don't want to stereotype any age group because in my opinion nearly everyone involved in the mainstream crowd these days is a little crazy. I'll thank social media and Covid-19 for that. LOL!

I'm the kind of guy that just likes to mind this own business, say "Ok" to controversial stuff to avoid problems, and remember the old days to stay mentally healthy. I like to talk or chat with like-minded people. And for the younger crowd who wasn't around back in the day, but support the old school feeling..... Welcome!

I could go on and on about how the world has changed, but I'm too lazy. I think we all know already.

Listening to older music seems to bring back good memories and relax people. You can choose your favorite songs and EASILY add them to the playlist or JUST listen. There is no perfect song, but most people agree that old songs bring back good memories.

Don't forget to bookmark the event link. :)

Stay tuned......

jsonld_parsed.description:
**📢IMPORTANT : CHECK THE SESSION TIME IN OUR WEBSITE(The time on the website and the meetup site may not match since we change it ocasionally)**

**Hi there! My name is Chloe.**
I'm a certified English teacher from United States.
I wanted to make an online language club where people can practice foreign languages by having real casual conversation!
I'm looking for people who want to practice conversational English by talking about interesting topics and hanging out with people from all over the world in a small online group.
**Here are some examples of what our weekly topics might be like:**
**"What would you do if you come across your crush?"**
**"Have you ever done the MBTI test? If so, what is your personality type?"**
**"Do you believe in love at first sight? Why or why not?"**
**"What are you most worried about right now?**
💎Here are some details💎
✔️ We meet via Zoom
✔️ The session will last for 1 hour and consists of 3 different rounds
✔️ Each round has different topics and discussion questions
✔️ Each round, the groups are randomly mixed, so you will have a chance to talk to different people every time
✔️ This isn't just about practicing English, but also about listening to different opinions and learning about different cultures
**✔️ The participation is FREE**
**❌ No credit card**
**❌ No Ads**

**📢IMPORTANT : CHECK THE SESSION TIME IN OUR WEBSITE(The time on the website and the meetup site may not match since we change it ocasionally)**

💎 How to Join 💎

1. [Click the link(here)](https://langclub.live/sessions)
2. [Sign up](https://langclub.live/signup)

3\. Click 'book' in the session that you want to participate\.
4\. Show up at the session time and click 'Join' in the session page
(The Zoom invitation will be sent to your e-mail once you apply too)
5\. Enjoy practicing English with people from all over the world\!
